stem: In which section of the statement of cash flows is the purchase of a new delivery vehicle shown?

options.rationale: Correct: buying non-current assets is investing.
Operating activities arise from the normal trading of the business.
Financing relates to shares, loans and dividends.

options.content: It is not shown, because it is not an expense
options.rationale: All cash flows are shown, whether or not they are expenses.

explanation: Purchases of property, plant and equipment are cash outflows from investing activities.

stem: Dividends paid to shareholders are shown in the statement of cash flows under:

options.rationale: Correct: they are a return to the providers of finance.
Dividends are not part of operating cash flow in this syllabus.
Dividends paid are not an investment.
Dividends are not deducted in arriving at operating cash.

explanation: Dividends paid are a financing outflow. Dividends received on investments are an investing inflow.

stem: A company issues ordinary shares of US\$1 for cash at a premium. What is shown in financing activities?

options.rationale: The premium is also received in cash.

options.content: The total cash received, including the premium
options.rationale: Correct: the premium is also cash from shareholders.
The nominal value is also received.

options.content: Nothing, because shares are not a cash flow
options.rationale: A share issue for cash is a financing inflow.

explanation: Proceeds of a share issue are nominal value plus premium.

stem: The cost of property, plant and equipment was US\$210,800 at the start of the year and US\$262,300 at the end. Equipment which cost US\$25,400 was sold during the year. What was the cash paid for new property, plant and equipment, assuming all purchases were for cash?

options.rationale: The cost of the equipment sold was not added back.
The cost of the equipment sold was deducted a second time.
The opening cost was ignored.

hints: Closing cost = opening cost + purchases - cost of disposals.

stem: How is a bank overdraft that is repayable on demand treated in the statement of cash flows?

options.content: As an inflow from financing activities
options.rationale: An overdraft is part of cash equivalents.

options.content: As an expense of the operating activities
options.rationale: The overdraft balance is not an expense.

options.content: As an outflow from investing activities
options.rationale: It has nothing to do with investing.

options.content: As a negative part of cash and equivalents
options.rationale: Correct: it is netted with cash and bank.

explanation: Under IAS 7 an overdraft repayable on demand forms part of cash and cash equivalents.
hints: Which total does the statement reconcile?

stem: Net cash from operating activities was US\$41,300, net cash used in investing activities US\$52,600 and net cash from financing activities US\$18,200. What was the net change in cash and cash equivalents?

options.rationale: The signs of the three totals have been reversed.
The investing outflow was added the wrong way.
The financing inflow was deducted.

hints: Add the three net totals, with the investing total negative.

stem: A company issued 36,000 ordinary shares of US\$1 at US\$1.60 each. It also repaid loan notes of US\$25,000 at par. What is the net cash flow from these two financing items?

options.rationale: The cash paid to repay the loan notes has been ignored.
Only the nominal value of the new shares has been counted.
Correct: 57,600 received less 25,000 repaid.
The cash received from the new issue has been ignored.

explanation: Received 36,000 × 1.60 = 57,600; repaid 25,000; net inflow 32,600.
hints: Work out the inflow and the outflow separately.

stem: Which statement about the statement of cash flows of a sole proprietor (ZIMSEC) is correct?

options.content: Drawings are deducted in operating activities
options.rationale: Drawings are withdrawals of capital, not operating costs.

options.content: Income tax paid is shown in operating activities
options.rationale: A sole proprietor's business pays no income tax.

options.content: Drawings are shown in financing activities and there is no tax
options.rationale: Correct: the owner's withdrawals replace dividends.
Loans and drawings are financing items.

explanation: A sole proprietor's business has no income tax and no dividends; drawings and capital introduced are financing flows.
hints: What replaces dividends for a sole proprietor?

stem: Interest received is shown in investing activities.
explanation: True. Interest and dividends received are returns on investments and are shown as investing inflows.

stem: The closing figure in the statement of cash flows must equal the bank and cash balances in the closing statement of financial position, taking account of any overdraft.
explanation: True. The statement explains the change in cash and cash equivalents, so the closing figure must agree with the statement of financial position.

stem: Match each cash flow to its section of the statement of cash flows.

left.content: Proceeds of sale of a machine

explanation: Sale of assets is investing; loan repayment and dividends are financing; tax paid is deducted in operating activities.

stem: Complete the sentences about the statement.

payload.template: Net cash from operating, investing and financing activities gives the net {{blank:a}} in cash and cash equivalents. Adding the {{blank:b}} balance gives the closing balance.

explanation: The three net totals give the net change, which is added to the opening balance to find the closing balance.

stem: State the section of the statement of cash flows in which interest paid on loan notes is deducted (under the syllabus convention used in this course).
explanation: Interest paid and tax paid are deducted after cash generated from operations in operating activities.

stem: Retained earnings were US\$18,900 at the start of the year and US\$29,450 at the end. The profit for the year was US\$21,200. There were no transfers to other reserves. Calculate the dividends paid in the year (no dividends were payable at either date).

Income tax payable was US\$4,600 at the start of the year and US\$5,300 at the end. The income tax charge in the statement of profit or loss was US\$12,700. Calculate the tax paid shown in the statement of cash flows.
explanation: Tax paid = 4,600 + 12,700 - 5,300 = 12,000. Using the charge gives 12,700.
workedSolution: 1. Tax paid = 4,600 + 12,700 - 5,300 = 12,000. Using the charge gives 12,700.
hints: Build the tax payable account: opening + charge - paid = closing.

stem: Cash and cash equivalents were US\$8,750 at the start of the year. Net cash from operating activities was US\$26,400, net cash used in investing activities US\$37,900 and net cash from financing activities US\$13,150. Calculate the cash and cash equivalents at the end of the year.
State two reasons why a business that makes a profit may still have a net decrease in cash.

points.description: Cash was spent on non-current assets, loan repayments, tax or dividends, which do not reduce profit before tax
Profit was tied up in higher inventory and trade receivables

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Cash may be spent on new assets, loans, tax and dividends. Profit may also be tied up in inventory and receivables.

explanation: One mark for each reason.

stem: Explain why the cash flow statement is useful to the bank manager who is considering a loan to a company.

points.description: It shows whether operations generate enough cash to pay interest and repay a loan
It shows how the company finances investment, from operating cash or from borrowing
Unlike profit, cash flows cannot be affected by accounting policies such as depreciation

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The bank manager can see whether the operations produce enough cash to pay interest and repay a loan. The statement also shows how investment is financed, and cash is less open to accounting choices than profit.

explanation: One mark each for servicing the loan, the source of finance and reliability of cash.
hints: Which of the three sections matters most to a lender?

stem: A company had net cash from operating activities of US\$18,000, net cash used in investing activities of US\$55,000 and net cash from financing activities of US\$41,000. Evaluate its position and advise the directors.

points.description: Operating cash is positive but small compared with the US\$55,000 spent on investing, so the investment is mostly financed from outside
Financing of US\$41,000 (loans or shares) covers the gap, which increases the company's debt or ownership
The investment may raise future operating cash, which would make the position acceptable
Advice: check the return on the new assets, and keep borrowing at a level that operating cash can service

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Operating cash of US\$18,000 pays for only a third of the US\$55,000 investment, so the company depends on US\$41,000 of new finance. That is acceptable only if the new assets raise operating cash. The directors should check the returns and avoid excessive borrowing.

explanation: One mark each for the comparison, the reliance on financing, a balancing point and advice.
hints: Compare operating cash with the investing outflow.

stem: Chipo Ncube runs a bakery in Chinhoyi as a sole proprietor. At 1 January 2025 she had: property, plant and equipment at cost US\$64,000 with accumulated depreciation US\$22,800; inventory US\$7,500; trade receivables US\$5,200; bank US\$3,100; trade payables US\$6,900; a loan US\$15,000. In 2025 her net profit was US\$18,400 after charging depreciation of US\$5,200 and loan interest of US\$1,350 (paid in full). She bought equipment for US\$12,500 cash, repaid US\$3,000 of the loan and withdrew US\$11,200. Inventory fell by US\$800, trade receivables rose by US\$1,600 and trade payables rose by US\$900.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the cash generated from operations.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the net cash from operating activities.
parts.explanation: 25,050 - interest paid 1,350 = 23,700. A sole proprietor pays no income tax.
parts.workedSolution: 1. 25,050 - interest paid 1,350 = 23,700. A sole proprietor pays no income tax.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the net cash used in financing activities. Enter an outflow as a negative number.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate the cash and cash equivalents at 31 December 2025.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Explain why drawings are shown in financing activities and not in operating activities.

points.description: Drawings are withdrawals of capital by the owner, not a cost of running the business
They are a payment to the provider of finance, like a dividend to shareholders

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Drawings are the owner taking back capital, not an expense of trading. They are a return to the provider of finance, so they belong in financing.

explanation: This item tests a sole proprietor's statement of cash flows.
hints: Add back the interest, then deduct it as interest paid.
No tax is paid by a sole proprietor.
